intro: Veshamarta et hammitzva veet hachuqqim veet hammishpatim asher anoki metzavveka hayyom laasotam (debarim z, y), nireh li bs"d deyadua try"g mitzot hem shelosha minim yesh niqraim chuqqim sheen lahem taam veen hassekel mechayyeb otam, veyesh niqraim mitzot bistam sheyyesh lahem taam, ak en hassekel mechayyeb otam sheim lo tzivvanu hashshem yitbarak lo hayinu osim otam middatenu, veyesh niqraim mishpatim sheyyesh lahem taam vehassekel mechayyeb otam sheggam im lo hayinu metzuvvim meet hashshem yitbarak hayinu mechuyyabim leqayyemam middatenu veyadua dei epshar leadam echad leqayyem kol hattarya"g mitzot bepoal ak "y hammachashaba shehu yosheb umetzappeh ematay tabo lide mitzva zo vaaqayyemenna o halvay shehayiti shayyak bemitzva zo vaaqayyemenna nechshab lo bazeh keillu qiyyem kullam ulepi zeh epshar shebbeyom echad yeqayyem haadam kol try"g mitzot im yihyeh machsheb al kol mitzva bipne atzmah vezeh shekkatub "veshamarta et hammitzva" milleshon "veabiv shamar et haddabar" (bereshit lz, y) shettihyeh metzappeh lemin hanniqra beshem mitzva bistam ulemin hanniqra beshem chuqqim ulemin hanniqra beshem mishpatim deellu hem kelalut kol try"g mitzot hinneh bazeh tarvicha apillu hayyom hazzeh kelomar beyom echad bilbad nechshab leka keillu asitem bepoal:

Nimtza detarya"g mitzot hem shelosha minin hanniqraim mitzot vechuqqim umishpatim kaasher peret otam hakkatub kan ukeneged shelosha mine mitzot ellu natan hshy"t laadam shelosha mine hanaa: haechad - hanaat hattaam shehu bappeh vehashsheni - hanaat harecha hattob shehu bachotem, vehashshelishi - hanaat mareh hattob shehu baenayim, ushelashettam metzuyim baggashmiyyut baolam hazzeh ak iqqar hanaa sheyyichyeh bah haadam baolam hazzeh hu hanaat akila ushetiyya shehi bappeh sheomed tachton ukesheyyiptor haadam meolam hazzeh hattachton titbattel mimmennu hanaa zo shebbappeh veyichyeh began eden bahanaat harecha ki sham began eden hattachton titlabbesh hannepesh begup mammash ak hu chomer zak sheeno tzarik laakila ushetiyya ella yichyeh veyitqayyem al hanaat harecha hattob shemmericha began eden hattachton kannoda vekatabti besipre haq' rab pealim dezehu hattaam denohagin poh irenu bagdad y" shebbetok shenem asar chodesh mebiim yoreshe hanniptar me veradim o shoshannim o mine asabim sheyyesh lahem recha tob veochazim otam veomedim bepetach bet hakkeneset kede sheyyebareku hanniknasin vehayyotzeim gam darkam lehachazir otam al kol haqqahal sheyyebareku alehem umishtaddelim lezakkot et harabbim tamid babboqer ubaereb bibraka zo shel harecha betok shenem asar chodesh mippene dehanniptar napsho began eden hattachton desham neheneh venizzon min harecha hattob lekak toil lo birkat harecha bimnuchat napsho yoter mishshear berakot gam yesh taam bebirkat harecha limnuchat nepesh hanniptar mippene ki gam bihyoto bachayyim chayyuto baolam hazzeh yesh hanaa lanneshama min harecha, kemo sheameru ribbatenu za"l (berakot mg:) al happasuq (tehillim rn, v): "kol hanneshama tehallel yah" ezehu dabar shehanneshama nehenet bo zeh harecha veha beha talya dehanneshama nehenet min harecha baolam hazzeh mippene shezzehu mazon shellah aach"k began eden, vesham beseper haq' hannizkar haaleti bitshuba leotam hannohagim lehaamid bebet haabel adam omed besamuk lappetach ubeyado keli me veradim kede sheyyebareku habbaim sham bitziatam en bazeh mishshum chashash mishshum ha dekatab beshulchan aruk yoreh dea siman sh"ch seip ch', dehatam ayre lehabi lipne hayyoshebim etzel haabel besamim o mugmar shehu taanug shel simcha dela shayyak zeh beabel mah sheen ken zeh shettopes keli shel me veradim beyado harachoq etzel bet haabel shekkol echad mebarek umericha leatzmo zeh nikkar sheosin bishbil habberakot limnuchat nepesh hanniptar veen kan chashash hannizkar:

Veachar aliyya shel gan eden hattachton yesh aliyya gedola mimmenna shehi began eden haelyon vesham hanneshama nizzonet biriyya shemmistakkelet beziv hashshekina veal zeh amo rabbotenu za"l (berakot yz.): olam habba en bo akila ushetiyya ella tzaddiqim yoshebim veatrotehem berashehem venehenin mizziv hashshekina vehu hanaa baenayim shellahem velaken asa hashshem yitbarak shelosha ebarim ellu - peh chotem ayin - zeh lemala mizzeh kepi seder madregot hahanaot sheyyesh laadam bezeh achar zeh kaamur. ubazeh perashti bs"d remez hakkatub (bereshit mt, mb) "ben porat yosep ben porat ale ayin" ki hatztzaddiq niqra yosep al derek sheamo rabbotenu zikronam libraka (shabbat qnb.): talmide chakamim kol zeman shemmazqinin datan mittosepet alehem veachar olam hazzeh hu ben porat began eden sheyyesh lo chen mechuddash bahanaato lihyot nizzon min harecha veachar chen zeh od yesh lo chen nosap vezehu ben porat ale ayin sheyyihyeh nizzon veneheneh biriyyat haayin vezehu taklitat hanaato:

Velaken tzarik haadam lehizzaher baolam hazzeh bipgam hammaggia leenayv yoter mikkol haebarim yaan ki kol eber shechote haggup bo hinneh hu pogem kenegdo beeber shel nishmato umeachar shettaklit hammaala shel hanaat nishmat haadam hu baenayim lekak tzarik leqaddesh uletaher haenayim shello bihyoto baolam hazzeh yoter mikkol ebarim shello:

Ubazeh muban inyan hammaaseh derabbi matya ben charash shehebi baal "seder haddorot" (ch"b erek r' matya b"ch) beshem midrash abkir (bylq"sh parashat vaychi lappasuq hanna"l) vezeh leshono: rabbi matya ben charash haya yosheb bebet hammidrash veoseq battora veziv panayv domot lachmah uqelaster panayv lemalake hashsharet mippene shemmemayv lo nasa enayv beishsha paam achat abar satan venitqanne bo amar epshar adam kazeh lo chata amar lipne hqb"h ribbono shel olam rabbi matya ben charash ma hu lepaneka amar lo tzaddiq gamur hu amar lo ten li reshut veassitennu amar lo en atta yakol lo vp"k lek halak venidmeh lo keishsha yapa shello haya kidmutah leolam memot naama achot tubal qayin (bereshit d, kb) shettau bah hammalakim hannepilim veamad lepanayv kevan sheraahu hapak panayv laachorayv veamad letzad semol vehapak panayv leyamin vehaya mithappek lekol tzad amar rabbi matya mityare ani shemma yitgabber alay yitzri veyachatieni qara letalmid shehaya mesharet lepanayv veamar lo lek vehabe li esh umasmer vehebi lo ubier hammasmer baesh unetano beenayv venistamme ukesheraa hassatan kak nizdaza venapal laachorayv beotah shaa qara hqb"h lemalak repael veamar lo lek verappo et matya ben charash ba veamad lepanayv amar lo mi atta amar lo repael sheshshelachani hqb"h leriput eneka amar lo hannicheni mah shehaya haya chazar lipne hqb"h amar lo kak vekak amar li amar lo hqb"h lek veemor lo ani areb shello yishlot bo yitzhar hara miyyad rippe oto ad kan. vekatab harab za"l sham middibre hamqubbalim za"l vezeh leshono: rabbi matya ben charash haya palti ben layish shellaqach et mikal bat shaul venaatz chereb beno lebeno (sanhedrin yt:) veim kol zeh lo haya lo leakkebah dehaya lo lemor leshaul hammelek alayv hashshalom: en ani rotzeh liqqach otah ubemaqom sheyyesh chillul hashshem en choleqin kabod larab (berakot yt:) veal zeh neemar (mika b, t): "neshe immi tegareshu mibbet taanugeha" v"p shello naga bah mikkol maqom beal karecho neheneh mimmarit ayin shezzanu enayv bemah sheeno shello ki etzlo hayeta yoshebet veshokebet velaken ratza atta letaqqen dabar zeh venitgalgel inyan zeh leyado kede sheyyetzaer atzmo veyeor enayv: ubaabur zeh nimsar battechilla beyad hassatan lehassito vehu nitazzer neged yitzro velo ratza lehabbit bepaneha ushenehem palti umateya hayu nitzotz yosep hatztzaddiq alayv hashshalom ad kan leshono yeuyyan sham: vehinneh bazeh haddabar shekkekatab harab za"l beshem hamqubbalim za"l yesh letaretz bs"d diqduq gadol sheyyesh bemaamar hannizkar deamar hassatan epshar adam kazeh lo chata denireh middebarayv adam kazeh rauy sheyyecheta ulehaki qa matmah ubeemet haddabar lehepek deadam kazeh shehu tzaddiq gamur rauy shello yecheta, ak yuban bs"d hainyan al pi mah shekkatab rabbenu haari"y za"l bemaamar (shabbat qych:) abuk bemay zehir tepe? shehayu shoalim chakme hattalmud zeh lazeh . dehakkavvana hu kol tzaddiq sheyyabo begilgul kede letaqqen dabar echad yihyeh nizhar beoto haddabar betaklit umoser atzmo alayv ukemo inyan bereh derab sapera bazzohar teruma (dap qsv.) shehishlik atzmo min haggag kede laanot qaddish vehaynu bishbil shebba begilgul baabur oto inyan velaken hayu hachakamim shoalin zeh mizzeh abuk bemay zehir tepe kede shebbazeh yakkiru bishbil ezeh dabar ba begilgul vekannizkar kol zeh beshaar haggilgulim yeuyyan sham vehinneh hassatan raa derabbi meir alayv hashshalom haya nizhar beinyan hahistakkelut betaklit ki miqqatnuto haya nishmar shello lirot pene ishsha apillu behaabara bealema veraa shehaya lo bazeh haddabar chasidut niplaa shello nimtzet bishar tzaddiqim lekak amar adam kazeh shehu mitchassed biriyyat hannashim chasidut niplaa shennizhar meod yoter mechaberayv epshar haya zeh etzlo al magen, shello chata bedabar zeh shel histakkelut begilgul haqqodem ki hassatan yodea dishmira veazhara bedabar echad yoter min rauy hi mokachat shebbaggilgul haqqodem chata bedabar zeh ukemo shekkatab beshem rabbenu haari"y za"l leel velaken achar shehikricha mitztzad shaqul haddaat devadday chata bidbar hahistakkelut begilgul haqqodem o chashab shevvadday atta begilgul zeh yukal lehachtio bedabar zeh ulekak nidmeh lo keishsha yapa meod veim kol zeh lo yakol lo nimtza lepi haamur depalti hutzrak lehitgalgel velisbol tzaar haggadol hazzeh shel ivvaron enayim sheivver otam beyadayim begachelet shel barzel shehu tzaar dei epshar laadam lesabelo, vekol zeh baabur hazanat enayim shello shezzanu min reiyyat ishsha sheenah shello beal karecho veshello birtzono, vehaddabar yippale al meh hayeta kol hacharada hazzot shehutzrak lehitgalgel kede lisbol tzaar haggadol hazzeh, ak kepi haamur muban shappir mippene shettaklit hanaat hatztzaddiqim vahazanatam hu baenayim shellahem began eden haelyon lekak tzarik ledaqdeq bedabar hannogea leenam apillu baabur dabar qal kechut hassaara lisbol alayv tzaar qasheh umar meod kede lenaqqotam ulezukkekem heteb heteb legamre:

Vehinneh kebar amarnu d"g deiqqar chayyot haadam baolam hazzeh teluya bahanaa shebbappeh shehu akila ushetiyya, im kol zeh natan hqb"h laadam baolam hazzeh hanaa berecha hachotem, vahanaa biriyya baenayim, ulekak bekol shelosha mine hanaot ellu tiqqenu chakamenu zikronam libraka berakot, mippene ki hayyetzer hara mitgareh yoter beeber sheyyesh bo hanaa laadam, v"y habberakot asher nitqenu bahanaot shelosha ebarim ellu az nishmarim ebarim ellu minnezeq hayyetzer hara hammitgareh bahem, ulekak kemo shennitqenu berakot al akila ushetiyya shebbappeh, kak nitqenu berakot al harecha shebbachotem, veken nitqenu gam ken berakot al reaya shebbaenayim vekaasher nebaer hilkotehem bashshabbat habbaa beezrat hashshem yitbarak:

paragraphs: Al hanaat harecha tzarik lebarek vesameku zeh aqqera bappasuq "kol hanneshama tehallel yah" (tehillim qnv, v), ezehu dabar shehanneshama nehenet mimmennu zeh harecha (berakot mg:), d"p shehaggup name neheneh mimmennu im kol zeh hanaat hanneshama min harecha hi yoter merubba mehanaat haggup ki hanaat haggup mistalleqet tekep umiyyad kesheyyaabor harecha abal hanaat hannepesh min harecha matmedet venisheret kochah bah, umittaam zeh en mebarekin al harecha beraka acharona mippene ki etzel haggup hanaa muetet hi sheoberet mimmennu tekep vedame laakila sheen mebarekin aleha beraka acharona achar haikkul shennitakkela, umittaam zeh gam ken en mebarekin shehecheyanu al harecha "p shehu besamim asher yitchaddeshu mishshana leshana, mippene shehanaat harecha etzel haggup hi hanaa muetet, v"p sheetzel hannepesh hi hanaa merubba lo shayyak lebarek shehecheyanu baabur hanaat hannepesh ki hannepesh nitzchit velo tamut velo shayyak legabbe didda beraka shel shehecheyanu vekannizkar bapposeqim za"l:

clarification.explanation: For enjoying a pleasant smell one must recite the first berachah [beforehand]. The Sages derived this from the verse "Let every soul praise the Lord," because smell is something the soul especially enjoys. Although the body also benefits from smell, the soul's enjoyment is greater and lasts longer, while the body's enjoyment passes the moment the smell is gone. Because the body's enjoyment from smell is small and fleeting, the Sages did not institute a concluding berachah (borei nefashot) over smell, similar to eating, after which no concluding berachah is recited once the food has been digested. For the same reason, one also does not recite Shehecheyanu over spices that are renewed from year to year, since the body's enjoyment from them is minor, and for the soul, which is eternal, Shehecheyanu does not apply.
takeaways: For enjoying a pleasant smell one must recite the appropriate first berachah.
No concluding berachah is recited over smell.
Shehecheyanu is not recited over new spices.

paragraphs: Asur lehanot mericha tob ad sheyyebarek qodem sheyyaricha, veim hu mesuppaq im bedabar zeh yesh recha tob o lav, o im hu mesuppaq beatzmo im yargish berecha ki lipamim yihyeh laadam choli nshl"h (nazzelet) velo yargish chush harecha shello, hare zeh mericha qodem kede leda veaach"k yebarek veyaricha kede shello tihyeh birkato lebattala vekannizkar bechesed lealpayim:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden to enjoy a pleasant smell before reciting the berachah beforehand. And if one is uncertain whether the object has a pleasant smell, or is uncertain about himself as to whether he will be able to sense the smell (for instance, one who has a cold) — he should smell it first in order to find out, and only afterward recite the berachah and smell it [properly], so that his berachah should not be recited in vain (Chesed LeAlafim).
takeaways: It is forbidden to enjoy a pleasant smell before reciting the berachah.

When uncertain whether there is a smell or whether one will be able to sense it (e.g. due to a cold), one should smell it first to check, and then recite the berachah and smell it [properly] (so the berachah is not in vain).

paragraphs: Yittol habbesamim beyado hayyemanit vibarek, ukemo shekkatabti leel gabbe beraka shel akila ushetiyya shetztzarik littol beyamin dabar shehu mebarek alayv, ubeseper keter malkut ketibat yad katub tob shehaadam yargil atzmo bekol paam sheyyaricha lomar beet shemmericha pasuq zeh, vehu: "recha nechuch ishsha lah'", mippene shebbepasuq zeh nirmezu kol kavvanot shel harecha, veyargil bekak ben bechol ben beshabbat:

clarification.explanation: When reciting a berachah over spices, one should take the spices in the right hand and recite the berachah over them, as we already wrote regarding berachot over eating and drinking — that one must hold in the right hand the item over which he is reciting the berachah. It is written in the manuscript of Sefer Keter Malchut that it is good to accustom oneself, every time one smells, to recite at the moment of smelling the verse: "Rei'ach nicho'ach isheh laHashem" ("a sweet savor, a fire-offering to the Lord"), because this verse alludes to all the intentions connected with smell. One should make this a habit both on weekdays and on Shabbat.
takeaways: One should hold the spices in the right hand when reciting the berachah over the smell.
It is good to recite the verse "Rei'ach nicho'ach isheh laHashem" every time one smells [spices], both on weekdays and on Shabbat.

paragraphs: Birkat akila ushetiyya qodemet lebirkat harecha, vehaynu davqa im shenehem lepanayv, abal orechim shebbaim bebet beelem habbayit umebiim lahem mine besamim techilla, veaach"k mebiim lahem mashqeh o perot en tzerikin lehamtin ella yebareku tekep al habbesamim shellipnehem:

clarification.explanation: When a person has before him both food or drink and something with a pleasant smell, he must recite the berachah over the food or drink first, and only afterward over the smell. But guests who come to a house, and are first served spices to smell and only afterward given a drink or fruit, need not wait — rather they should recite the berachah immediately over the spices before them.
takeaways: If food/drink and spices are before you together, recite the berachah over the food/drink first.
If you are a guest and were served spices first, recite the berachah immediately over the spices — no need to wait for the food.

paragraphs: Im zeh shehu mericha bo hu etz o yotze min haetz mebarek alayv bore atze besamim, veim hu eseb mebarek isbe besamim, veim eno lo etz velo eseb kemo mys"k (moseq - shemen hammor) o mb"r (tablin haddi charip) vekayyotze mebarek mine besamim, veken im hu mesuppaq bo ben etz leeseb o sheyyesh bo machaloqet yebarek bore mine besamim, ki beraka zo shel mine besamim hu keneged beraka shel shehakkol sheamarnu gabbe akila: vehassiman leda ulehabchin ben min etz leben min eseb zeh hakkelal kol shehaqqelach shello qasheh venishar haqqelach mishshana leshana veen alayv yotzein mishsharashayv ella miggizo vekol shekken meetzayv hare zeh min etz lekulle alema, umebarek alayv atze besamim, vekol shehaqqelach shello rak keyaraq o apillu shehu qasheh eno nishar haqqelach mishshana leshana hare zeh min eseb umebarek isbe, veyesh omerim daapillu im haqqelach rak im hu nishar mishshana leshana hare zeh min etz, vekol keha deyesh machaloqet yebarek mine besamim:

clarification.explanation: When a person smells something fragrant, the berachah depends on the source of the smell: if the source is a tree or something that grows on a tree, one recites "Borei atzei vesamim." If the source is a plant [herb], one recites "Borei isvei vesamim." If the source is neither a tree nor a plant (such as musk or ambergris, and the like), or there is doubt or dispute whether it is a tree or a plant, one recites "Borei minei vesamim." The rule for identification: a plant whose stalk is hard, remains from year to year, and whose leaves grow from the trunk or branches, is considered a tree. A plant whose stalk is soft like a vegetable, or even hard but does not remain from year to year, is considered a plant [herb]. Some hold that even a soft stalk that remains from year to year is considered a tree, and in such a case of dispute one recites "Borei minei vesamim."
takeaways: For a smell from a tree or from what grows on it — the berachah "Borei atzei vesamim."
For a smell from a plant [herb] — the berachah "Borei isvei vesamim."
In case of doubt, dispute, or when the source of the smell is neither tree nor plant — the berachah "Borei minei vesamim."

paragraphs: Al haqqalabiina sheqqorin bearbe vered el qnpy"l (vered sicha rechane) mebarekin atze besamim, v"g dibseper zekor leabraham hebi beshem meam loez (parashat toledot) lebarek mine mishshum shehu sapeq, hinneh zeh haggadel poh irenu bgd"d y" en bo sapeq yaan haqqelach shello qasheh veen healin yotzein min hashsharashin vegam hu nishar mishshana leshana, veken al qrnp"l (tzipporen) habba mimmedinat hayyam yebareku atze besamim deken hamminhag pashut poh irenu y" mizzeman ateret rashe harab mv"r zeqeni rabbenu mosheh chayyim za"l keshehayu holekin qahal rab lehishtatteach bekol shana al matztzebet yechezqel hannabi "h sheshsham en hadas umebarekin behabdala bemotzae shabbat al qrnp"l atze besamim, veken asu keshehaleku libroach bizman haddabar, lo taqum paamayim tzara, vezeh hamminhag barur upashut poh irenu:

clarification.explanation: Over the flower of the fragrant rose bush called "ward el-qanfil" one recites "Atzei vesamim." Although there is an opinion in Sefer Zechor LeAvraham that raises a doubt and suggests reciting "Minei vesamim," here in our city of Baghdad there is no doubt, because its stalk is hard, its leaves do not grow from the roots, and it endures from year to year. Similarly, over cloves (karanful) that come from abroad, one recites "Atzei vesamim," as is the simple custom in our city since the days of my grandfather, Rabbi Moshe Chaim, of blessed memory, who followed this custom for Havdalah at the close of Shabbat when there was no myrtle available, both when visiting the grave of the prophet Ezekiel and when fleeing during a plague. This custom is clear and well-established in our city.
takeaways: Over the fragrant rose bush (ward el-qanfil) one recites "Atzei vesamim."
Over cloves (karanful) one recites "Atzei vesamim," following the custom of Baghdad.

paragraphs: Al hz"r sheqqorin bearbi qd"ch (nitztzane perachim) hen shel etrog hen shel lymvny"m hen shel nryn"g (peri hadar qatan chimmutz) yebarek atze kemo shekkatab bizkur leabraham, veal havvered sheqqorin bearbe rsq"y (shoshanna rechanit) yebarek atze veken hamminhag pashut poh irenu:

clarification.explanation: When smelling flower buds, whether of etrog, lemon, or narinj (a small tart citrus fruit), one must recite "Borei atzei vesamim." The same law applies to the fragrant rose (called in Arabic "raski"), over which one recites "Borei atzei vesamim," and this is also the prevailing custom in our city.
takeaways: Over the blossoms of etrog, lemon, and narinj one recites "Borei atzei vesamim."
Over the fragrant rose as well, one recites "Borei atzei vesamim."

paragraphs: Al mynqsh"y (eseb bar rechane) sheqqorin bearbe bnpsh"h yebarek "mine" mishshum deyesh bazeh pelugta veken anachnu nohagim poh irenu lebarek al bnpsh"h "mine" bipne hassapeq, abal al eseb sheqqorin bearbe rych"n (eseb rechane) yebarek "isbe" lekulle alema, veal hrvd" sheqqorin bearbe sd"b nimtza poh irenu bgd"d en bo recha tob kelal veen mebarekin alayv kelum, veim hayu minim shel atze veisbe mechubbarim yachad baagudda achat veharecha shellahem yotze meurbab mishshenehem yebarek mine, abal im mubdalim baagudda sheyyukal letzamtzem bechatemo kol min bipne atzmo yebarek al kol min birkato:

clarification.explanation: Over a fragrant wild plant called in Arabic "banafsha" (violet), there is a halachic doubt, and therefore one recites over it "Borei minei vesamim." Such is the custom in Baghdad. Over a fragrant plant called in Arabic "reihan" [basil], one recites "Borei isvei vesamim" according to all opinions. Over a plant called in Arabic "sadab" [rue], there is no pleasant smell in Baghdad, and therefore no berachah is recited over it at all. If there is a bundle of tree-based and plant-based spices mixed together, and their smell emerges mixed together without the ability to distinguish, one recites "Borei minei vesamim." But if they are separated within the bundle and one can smell each species individually, he recites over each species its own appropriate berachah.
takeaways: Over "banafsha" [violet] one recites "Borei minei vesamim" out of doubt.
Over "reihan" [basil] one recites "Borei isvei vesamim."
Over "sadab" [rue], which lacks a pleasant smell, no berachah is recited.
In a mixed bundle of tree- and plant-based spices, one recites "Minei"; in a bundle where each can be smelled separately, one recites over each its own berachah.

paragraphs: Im bimqom atze o isbe o mine berak shehakkol nihyeh bidbaro yatza, veim berak al atze birkat isbe o bimqom isbe berak atze lo yatza, bammeh debarim amurim bemin shehu isbe lekulle alema vaatze lekulle alema vetaa bahem beet beraka, abal im haya zeh bemin sheyyesh disbira lehu beoto peri debirkato atze mippene siman echad shel atze nimtza, vaanachnu mebarekim alayv mine mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel deikka disbira lehu shetztzarik lebarek isbe hinneh im hattaut shel habberaka haya bazeh shebberak alayv atze o berak alayv isbe lo yachazor vibarek mine, mishshum dilman deamar zeh tzarik lebarek atze vehu berak atze, o lemaen demear zeh tzarik lebarek isbe vehu berak isbe yatza yede choba veek yachazor vibarek mine ha have beraka lebattala, ketzad yaaseh yeharher beraka shel mine belibbo veyaricha, o yebarek mine beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo veayyen chayye adam:

clarification.explanation: If, instead of reciting "Borei atzei vesamim" or "Borei isvei vesamim" or "Borei minei vesamim," one recited "Shehakol nihyeh bidvaro," he has fulfilled his obligation, since the berachah of "Shehakol" includes smell as well. But if he recited "Atzei" in place of "Isvei," or "Isvei" in place of "Atzei," he has not fulfilled his obligation. This applies specifically to a species that is a plant according to all opinions, or a tree according to all opinions, and he erred at the time of the berachah. But if it is a species disputed among the authorities (where some hold its berachah is "Atzei" because of a certain tree-like sign it has, and we recite "Minei" over it out of doubt, since others hold one should recite "Isvei") — if he mistakenly recited "Atzei" or "Isvei" over it (instead of the proper "Minei" recited out of doubt), he does not go back and recite "Minei": according to the opinion that holds one should recite "Atzei," he did recite "Atzei" and fulfilled his obligation; and according to the opinion that holds one should recite "Isvei," he did recite "Isvei" and fulfilled his obligation — and going back to recite "Minei" would be a berachah recited in vain. What should he do? He should contemplate the berachah of "Minei" in his heart and smell [the spices], or recite "Minei" without God's Name and Sovereignty, while contemplating the Name and Sovereignty in his heart.
takeaways: Mistakenly reciting "Shehakol" in place of "Atzei/Isvei/Minei vesamim" fulfills the obligation. Mistaking "Atzei" for "Isvei" in a species that is certain to all opinions does not fulfill it, and one must go back and recite the correct berachah.

For a species under halachic dispute (whose proper berachah is "Minei" out of doubt) — if one mistakenly recited "Atzei" or "Isvei," he does not go back and recite "Minei" (as that would be a berachah in vain); rather he contemplates "Minei" in his heart, or recites "Minei" without God's Name and Sovereignty while contemplating them in his heart.

paragraphs: Im yesh lepanayv min etz bevadday veod yesh min shehu sapeq atze sapeq isbe yebarek al hassapeq techilla birkat mine, veaach"k yebarek atze al etz vadday, veim yesh lepanayv min etz vadday umin isbe vadday veyesh od gam ken min acher shehu sapeq atze sapeq isbe im hu bachol yebarek al havvaddain vikavven liptor et min shehu sapeq, veim beshabbat yebarek al min hassapeq birkat mine techillat hakkol veaach"k yebarek atze al etz devadday vibarek isbe al eseb havvadday vekaasher katabti leel beparashat pinchas (halaka tz) gabbe birkat haakila yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: When a person has before him a spice that is certainly a tree, and also another spice that is doubtfully a tree or a plant, he first recites "Borei minei vesamim" over the doubtful one, and afterward recites "Borei atzei vesamim" over the certain tree. And if he has before him a certain tree, a certain plant, and also another species that is doubtfully a tree or a plant — on a weekday he recites the berachah over the certain ones and intends thereby to discharge the doubtful one as well; but on Shabbat he first recites "Borei minei vesamim" over the doubtful species, and only afterward recites "Borei atzei vesamim" over the certain tree and "Borei isvei vesamim" over the certain plant — as written above in Parashat Pinchas (Halachah 16) regarding the berachah over eating; see there.
takeaways: Certain tree + a species doubtful between tree and plant: recite "Borei minei vesamim" over the doubtful one first, then "Borei atzei vesamim" over the certain one.

Certain tree + certain plant + a doubtful species: on a weekday recite over the certain ones and intend to discharge the doubtful one; on Shabbat recite "Borei minei vesamim" over the doubtful one first, and only then "Borei atzei vesamim" and "Borei isvei vesamim" over the certain ones — as with the law of berachot over eating explained in Parashat Pinchas.

paragraphs: Im shalaq habbesamim vehotzi hashshemen mehem kederek shemmotzian shekar min hattemarim vekayyotze, mebarek al hayyotze beraka kayyotze bahem sheim habbesamim hem min etz yebarek atze veim eseb yebarek isbe, veshemen aparsemon mippene sheggadel beeretz yisrael qabeu lo beraka bipne atzmo lebarek bore shemen areb:

clarification.explanation: If one boiled spices and extracted oil from them — the way liquor is extracted from dates — one recites over the extracted oil the same berachah as over the spices themselves: if the spices are from a tree species, "Borei atzei vesamim," and if from a plant species, "Borei isvei vesamim." Balsam oil, because it grows in the Land of Israel, was given by the Sages its own special berachah — "Borei shemen arev" ("who creates pleasant oil").
takeaways: Oil extracted from spices receives the same berachah as its source (tree or plant).
Over balsam oil one recites the special berachah "Borei shemen arev."

paragraphs: Mebarekim al hammugmar dehaynu besamim sheosim al haggechalim leharicha bahem mishsheyyaaleh qitor ashano, abal lo yebarek qodem sheyyaaleh qitor ashano vegam bazeh habberaka kepi habbesamim im min etz atze veim min eseb isbe, bammeh debarim amurim hammugmar sheosin leharicha abal mah sheosin legammer bo hakkelim en mebarekin alayv kevan deen asuy leharicha beatzmo ella kede litten recha bekelim, veken hu haddin mah sheosin lirpua deen lebarek, vehu haddin name deen lebarek al besamim shenniknas bahem lebet hakkisse o shehubeu lehaabir hasserachon o lehaabir zuhamat hayyadayim:

clarification.explanation: One recites a berachah over "mugmar" — spices placed on coals in order to enjoy their smell — once the smoke begins to rise, but not before. Here too the berachah follows the type of spices (tree or plant). But this applies only to mugmar made in order to smell it; when it is made to scent garments or utensils, or for medicinal purposes, or to remove a bad odor from a room or from the hands — no berachah is recited, since it is not intended for enjoyment through smell itself.
takeaways: A berachah is recited over mugmar only once the smoke begins to rise.
No berachah is recited over scenting garments/utensils, medicinal smells, or removing a bad odor.

paragraphs: Besamim shemmunnachim becheder lischora apillu keshenniknas sham niknas leharicha en mebarek, veraq im notelan beyado yebarek alehem, mihu im niknas lachanut shel besamim venitkavven leharicha mebarek mishshum debachanut chashibi omedin leharicha denicha leh lebaal hachanut sheyyarichu bene adam veyiqnu mimmennu:

clarification.explanation: Spices kept in a room for commercial purposes — even if one enters that room specifically in order to smell them — one does not recite a berachah, unless he actually takes them in his hand. But one who enters a spice shop with the intention of smelling [the merchandise] does recite the berachah, because in a shop the spices are regarded as set up for smelling: the shopkeeper wants people to smell them, so that they will buy from him.
takeaways: Spices kept as merchandise — a berachah is recited only if one takes them in hand.
In a spice shop, one who enters to smell the merchandise recites the berachah.

paragraphs: Recha sheen lo iqqar kegon shehayu besamim munnachim bikli veqalat hakkeli et harecha venishsha bo recha tob kevan deen mammashut shel besamim bakkeli lo yebarek, vehu haddin im qelato etzbeotayv recha tob dela yebarek:

clarification.explanation: A smell that has no actual physical substance behind it — for example, spices that were kept in a vessel and the vessel absorbed their smell, so that a pleasant smell remains in it even though there is no longer any actual substance of spices in it — one does not recite a berachah over it, since there is no real substance of spices. The same applies if one's fingers absorbed a pleasant smell — no berachah is recited.
takeaways: No berachah is recited over a smell that lingers without the physical substance of the spices (an empty vessel that absorbed the scent, or scented fingers).

paragraphs: Kol peri harauy laakila veyesh bo recha tob im notelo leharicha bo, o apillu notelo leharicha bo uleakelo mebarek hannoten recha tob beperot, veyesh omerim im happeri omed laakila vehuba lepanayv leakelo sheim lo haya rotzeh leakelo lo haya mebio kede leharicha en lebarek alayv keshehu mericha veyesh lachush ledibrehem mishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel veen lebarek ella davqa im mebio lepanayv kede leharicha bo davqa, veken hamminhag pashut poh irenu kaasher mebiim lipnehem perot sheyyesh bahem recha tob laakila en merichim bahem kede shello yebareku al harecha, ulepi zeh adam choleh vekayyotze shemmebiim lo peri sheyyesh bo recha tob leharicha davqa velo leakelo tzarik lebarek lekulle alema ki zeh hu dina baggemara bibrakot dap m"g ammud b', vekaasher heeleti besipri haq' rab pealim mihu katabti sham sheanshe maaseh nimnaim milleharicha beshum paam bapperi apillu en rotzim leakelo ella raq leharicha, mippene sheyyesh pelugta benosach habberaka ki mera"n za"l beshulchan aruk udeimmeh sebira lehu lebarek hannoten recha tob beperot, ak eliyya raba seip qatan Adonai hebi hannussach mesappere harishonim za"l lebarek asher natan recha tob bapperot, veyesh soberim deikka qepida ben tere lishshane hannizkarim - veen mashmautam oleh beinyan echad, lepikak moshekin atzman milleharicha beshum peri bishbil hammebuka sheyyesh benussach habberaka.

clarification.explanation: A fruit fit for eating that has a pleasant smell — if one takes it in order to smell it (or to smell it and also eat it) — one recites "HaNoten rei'ach tov bepeirot." Some say that if the fruit is intended for eating and was brought to be eaten — such that had one not wanted to eat it, it would not have been brought merely for smelling — one should not recite a berachah over it when smelling it; and out of doubt regarding berachot, one should be lenient and not recite the berachah unless the fruit is brought specifically for the purpose of smelling it. Therefore the simple custom in our city, when fragrant fruits meant for eating are brought before people, is that they refrain from smelling them, so as not to recite a berachah over the smell. But a sick person, or someone similar, to whom a fragrant fruit is brought specifically for smelling and not for eating, must recite the berachah according to all opinions, as this is the ruling of the Gemara in Berachot 43b, as I raised in my book Rav Pe'alim. I wrote there, however, that people of pious deeds refrain from smelling fruit at all, even when they do not intend to eat it but only to smell it, because there is a dispute about the exact wording of the berachah (whether "HaNoten" or "Asher natan").
takeaways: A fragrant fruit brought specifically to be smelled — one recites "HaNoten rei'ach tov bepeirot."
A fruit brought for eating — one refrains from smelling it, out of doubt regarding the berachah.
People of pious deeds refrain from smelling fruit altogether, because of the dispute over the exact wording of the berachah.
